title: Djokovic Battles Back to Beat Zverev at the China Open
summary:
Novak Djokovic came back from a set down to beat top seed Alexander Zverev and reach the semi-finals of the China Open. Djokovic, a 39-year-old from Serbia, won the quarter-final 4-6 6-4 6-4 against Zverev, who is ranked number two in the world.

It was the first time the two had played each other in just under 16 months. At first, Djokovic struggled with Zverev's powerful game. Zverev, who is 29, won the first set after breaking Djokovic's serve in the first game. Then Djokovic fought his way back. He broke Zverev's serve at 5-4 in the second set to level the match. The third set was very close. Djokovic broke Zverev again at 5-4 to win. The result hurt Zverev's hopes of finishing the year as the world's number one player.

"These are the kind of moments that I still play for, compete for," Djokovic said. He added that the motivation is big when you are playing well against the best players in front of 15,000 people. "These are the kind of moments that define dreams, I think, of every tennis player."

The win extended Djokovic's unbeaten run in Beijing to 32 matches. He is now one step closer to a seventh China Open title and his first trophy of 2026. He has won 24 Grand Slam titles, but this year has been a hard one for him, with form and fitness proving challenging. "It's been a struggle this year for different reasons," he said. "But I'm still there, still grinding, still making the youngsters work for their money."

Djokovic will play third seed Daniil Medvedev in the semi-finals on Monday. Medvedev beat Francisco Cerundolo in his quarter-final. Hubert Hurkacz of Poland also reached the last four.
why_it_matters: The match shows how a veteran champion kept competing at the top level and how results can change the race for the year's top ranking.
